rules.statement: When a method writes output whose length the caller cannot know in advance (for example, a decrypted or unwrapped key that only a remote service's response reveals), take an `IBufferWriter<byte>` destination instead of a fixed `Memory<byte>`/`Span<byte>` destination with a returned byte count; keep `Span<byte>` plus `out int` only for results of known size.
rules.why: Callers who can't know the size end up guessing, for example renting twice the expected size. A result of the wrong length then fails as "destination too small" instead of reaching the caller's own size check.
rules.check: Look for new or changed APIs, especially async or interface methods backed by external services, that take a `Memory<byte>`/`Span<byte>` destination and return the bytes written while the output length depends on data the caller doesn't have. Also look for callers that over-rent buffers to work around this.
